Definition: , or feminine τηλικαύτη from a compound of G3588 with G2245 and G3778; such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast:--so great, so mighty.
BiblicalUsage: The word is so great, so vast, such as this. Paul says God delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver; the writer asks how we shall escape if we neglect so great salvation; and James says the ships, though they be so great and driven of fierce winds, are turned with a very small helm.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe so great is the measure of both the death and the salvation, and the small helm turns the great ship.
RelatedPeople: Paul; James, Brother of the Lord
